author: NorthEast News Desk
body: The Netherlands has signed a letter of intent with Sweden to acquire one Saab GlobalEye advanced surveillance aircraft, adding a national platform designed to monitor air, sea and land over long distances.

The Dutch government said Friday that the aircraft can detect threats including drones and cruise missiles while serving as a flying command center. It can distribute real-time intelligence to aircraft, ships and ground units, linking sensors and operators across multiple domains.

The Netherlands currently relies on NATO’s aging AWACS fleet because it lacks an aircraft for the mission. Delivery of the Dutch GlobalEye is expected in 2031, but the arrangement would give Dutch crews access to Swedish aircraft from 2028 for training and earlier operations.

The purchased aircraft would join a shared pool with three Swedish GlobalEye planes, allowing crews from both countries to use the fleet. The plan reflects rising European demand for airborne early-warning systems as militaries seek better detection of low-flying threats.
The letter of intent is an early procurement step. The initial announcement did not provide a purchase price or a schedule for completing the final contract.
dek: The planned aircraft would monitor air, sea and land, while access to Sweden’s fleet would let Dutch crews begin operating in 2028.
headline: Netherlands moves to buy Saab GlobalEye surveillance aircraft
